author: Maya Yang
description:
New report denounces Havana and claims ‘campaign of subversion’ has infiltrated highest levels of US government

As part of the Trump administration’s continuing attack on left-leaning groups, the US state department has listed several activists and organizations as “front groups and fellow travelers” for Cuba, including Hasan Piker and Amazon Labor Union founder Chris Smalls.

In a 100-page report released on Monday, the state department denounces Cuba as the “capital of 21st-century communism”, accusing the Cuban government of carrying out a “campaign of subversion” that has “infiltrated the highest reaches of the US government, recruited and cultivated generations of American activists [and] backed an unprecedented wave of leftwing terrorism on American soil”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Front groups and fellow travelers’: state department attacks US left over Cuba

author: Roque Planas
description:
United staffer told customer ‘you don’t act like at a citizen’ during incident over wait time at San Francisco airport

United Airlines is “looking into” a viral video showing a United Airlines employee threatening to call Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Mexican American man at San Francisco international Airport last week.

The scene erupted after Julio Varela of San Ramon grew upset at United Airlines staff for taking a long time to correct an error his family made when entering his daughter’s name to buy a ticket for flight to Canada, according to NBC News.
title: United Airlines says it will ‘look into’ worker’s threat to call ICE in viral video

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
President accused of having ‘lost control of this war’ as deaths of trio in Iranian military strikes fuel rising concern

Democrats have seized on the deaths of three US troops killed in Iranian strikes to urge Donald Trump to urgently reverse his resumption of the war with Iran amid widespread anxiety over climbing casualties.

Even as US forces launched a 10th consecutive wave of attacks against Iranian targets, concern over the deaths of American service personnel threatened to complicate moves to escalate the conflict, which has reignited after he last week walked away from a memorandum of understanding agreed with Iran in June.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It needs to end now’: Democrats urge Trump to halt Iran war after US troop deaths

author: Stephanie Convery
description:
One Nation MP grilled in 7.30 interview about Pauline Hanson’s podcast interview by far-right activist. Follow today’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australia Palestine Advocacy Network has criticised Labor’s draft policy platform on Palestine, saying it is “currently falling far short and does not acknowledge the Palestinian genocide”.

We reported this morning that Israel had made an intervention into the Labor party’s internal processes, publicly criticising the draft that it claims risks blaming Israel for the Gaza conflict while giving “insufficient attention” to the role of Hamas.

Despite what the Israeli Embassy might say, Labor is currently falling far short and does not acknowledge the P
title: Australia news live: Barnaby Joyce dogged by Tommy Robinson questions – and by a dog – in spiky ABC interview

author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
description:
Daniel Ortega, the 80-year-old authoritarian leader, says move will ‘build a wall’ against the opposition

Nicaragua’s long-serving president, Daniel Ortega, has said the country will hold no further elections to prevent the opposition from coming to power.

The 80-year-old authoritarian leader, who has been in office since 2007, also said he would work with the congress he controls to pass new laws that would “build a wall” against the opposition.

Continue reading...
title: Nicaragua’s president says country will not hold any more elections

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Turmoil likely as Trump officials say Canada unfairly discriminated against US autos, alcohol and dairy products

Donald Trump is imposing 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods, White House officials said on Monday, declaring Canada has unfairly discriminated against American autos, alcohol and dairy products.

The move could unleash a new wave of economic chaos, with risks of higher inflation and further fraying of relations between two nations that had been closely woven together before Trump’s return to the White House.

Continue reading...
title: Donald Trump to impose 50% tariff on most Canadian goods, White House says

author: Shrai Popat
description:
Interim senator appointed after Lindsey Graham’s death endorsed by Trump ‘for the Good of our Nation’

Darline Graham, the South Carolina interim senator and sister of the late Lindsey Graham, said she plans to run for a full Senate term after Donald Trump endorsed her last week.

In an interview with Sean Hannity that will air in full on Monday, Graham – who was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to finish the remainder of her brother’s term – said she had “made a decision”.

Continue reading...
title: Darline Graham, Lindsey Graham’s sister, to run for full Senate term

author: Maya Yang in New York
description:
Israeli prime minister is subject of an arrest warrant issued by international criminal court over alleged war crimes in Gaza

Donald Trump has said Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, “will not be arrested” if he visits the US.

His comments came days after Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, said he was exploring whether his administration could arrest Netanyahu if he visits the city during the UN general assembly in September.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says Benjamin Netanyahu ‘will not be arrested’ if he visits the US

author: Roque Planas
description:
A team of firefighters saved the pup from the water in a mission that utilized boats, trucks and a drone

Firefighters rescued a small dog that had been missing for weeks after finding it swimming into the San Francisco Bay.

The dog had gone missing over the Fourth of July weekend, according to the Menlo Park fire protection district. But someone called 911 on 16 July to say they had seen a dog enter the bay near the Dumbarton Bridge in East Palo Alto.

Continue reading...
title: Small dog missing for weeks rescued while swimming in San Francisco Bay

author: Associated Press
description:
The 18-year-old was found dead after a 4 July boat trip with his friends to an island in the Gulf coast

Family and supporters of Nolan Xavier Wells gathered in a Mississippi church on Monday to mourn and celebrate the 18-year-old, whose death following a 4 July boat trip with friends has captured national attention and prompted calls for an independent investigation.

The ceremony began with tearful remarks from Wells’s parents, who described their son as a warm and gentle presence, a gifted athlete and a role model to his younger siblings.

Continue reading...
title: Nolan Wells remembered at memorial as community demands truth about his death

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Jenitar Na’amoana’s already had four children when she learned of surprise pregnancy ‘unheard of’ in Australia

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A 34-year-old woman from Brisbane has defied the odds and delivered four naturally conceived, identical quadruplets in what is believed to be an Australian first.

Jenitar Na’amoana, who already had four children, was not planning having another but the quadruplets emerged from a “one in 15 million” pregnancy, splitting into four from a single fertilised egg.
title: ‘One in 15 million’: Brisbane woman gives birth to identical quadruplets

author: Associated Press
description:
Polarizing social media influencers are being held in federal detention in Miami as district judge considers extradition

Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate will fight extradition to the United Kingdom, their lawyer told a US magistrate in Miami on Monday after the brothers were arrested to face rape and sex-trafficking charges.

The Tates appeared in federal court for the first time since their arrest on Saturday and are being held in federal detention. In the coming weeks, a US district judge will consider whether they meet the conditions for extradition.

Continue reading...
title: Tate brothers fight extradition to UK over rape and sex-trafficking charges

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Scientists recorded slower reduction over past 20 years, but study finds this was ‘temporary rather than sustained’

A previously recorded slowdown in Arctic sea ice decline has ended, according to a new study, with the largest year-to-year wintertime reduction ever recorded.

In a study published last summer, researchers found that melting sea ice in the Arctic had slowed down over the past 20 years, with no statistically significant decline in its extent recorded between 2005 and 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Slowdown in Arctic ice melt ends after largest winter decline on record

author: Rowena Mason and Pippa Crerar
description:
Chancellor appointment and early policies avoid market meltdown but next week remains ‘moment of real peril’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has not quite gone for Keir Starmer’s extreme caution in the run-up to entering No 10 – but he is certainly aware that any early wrong moves would cost him.

Back in 2024, Starmer was criticised for his “Ming vase” strategy, where the leader treads very carefully so as not to drop a valuable metaphorical piece of china being carried across the room.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We need to be careful’: Andy Burnham’s team keenly aware of fiscal tightrope

author: Maya Yang
description:
Depression set to become tropical storm later on Monday as separate storm strengthens off Mexico’s Pacific coast

A tropical depression was continuing to develop along the US Gulf coast on Monday as Tropical Storm Fausto strengthened off Mexico’s south-west Pacific coast.

The National Hurricane Center (NHC) in Miami said that the depression was expected to become a tropical storm later on Monday, prompting new watches for portions of the Gulf region.

Continue reading...
title: Weather warnings as tropical depression develops along US Gulf coast

author: Shrai Popat
description:
Ex-Maine senate president is frontrunner to replace Platner, who ended his campaign after sexual assault allegations

Troy Jackson – a logger, longtime legislator and former president of the Maine senate – is now poised to become the Democratic nominee in Maine’s US Senate race. His rise comes after the party’s previous nominee, Graham Platner, abruptly ended his campaign earlier this month following allegations of sexual assault from a former partner.

Platner’s withdrawal set off a frantic scramble inside the Maine Democratic party. Several contenders filed paperwork to be considered at a 25 July special convention of 601 delegates tasked with selecting a new nominee. But over the weekend, Jackson’s serious challengers dropped out one after another, clearing a sw
title: Troy Jackson poised to replace Graham Platner as Democratic nominee in Maine Senate race

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Exclusive: Research spanning 82 countries finds antibiotic resistance increased in every region between 2004 and 2022

Harry Booth has had a rough run through Australia’s coldest months. The 13-year-old has been in and out of hospital with a range of common chest and urinary tract infections that his doctors find challenging to treat.

Harry was born with kidney failure and began dialysis at six months old, before receiving a kidney transplant from his father at age four. The surgery saved his life but comes with a trade-off: he now needs to take medications that suppress his immune system to prevent his body from rejecting the kidney.

Continue reading...
title: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria increasingly leaving children vulnerable to common infections, global study finds

author: Michael Sainato
description:
HHS failed to respond to Foia request following claims of fraud against Somali childcare providers and Democrats

Civil rights groups have sued the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) after the agency failed to respond to a Freedom of Information Act request regarding the Trump administration’s restrictions on federal childcare and family assistance following claims of fraud against Somali childcare providers and Democratic state officials.

The American Civil Liberties Union, the ACLU of Illinois, the ACLU of Colorado, the National Women’s Law Center, and the National Center for Law and Economic Justice, are seeking correspondence between federal officials and far right social media influencer Nick Shirley.

Continue reading...
title: Civil rights groups sue Trump administration over childcare funding restrictions

author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
description:
Additional £340m over three years allocated to get people off the streets ‘at the earliest opportunity’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has promised to end rough sleeping in England in his first pledge as prime minister, allocating an additional £340m over three years as he seeks to replicate the homelessness schemes he rolled out in Greater Manchester.

Speaking in front of Downing Street immediately after becoming prime minister, Burnham said he would try to get people off the streets “at the earliest opportunity”.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham pledges to end rough sleeping in England in first speech as prime minister

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Three people reported injured after incendiary device allegedly thrown at building also housing ICE field office

Authorities in New York City are investigating an explosion on Monday morning outside an FBI building in lower Manhattan that reportedly injured three people.

Investigators said a person who allegedly threw an incendiary device at the scene was taken into custody.

Continue reading...
title: Suspect held after explosion at FBI building in New York City

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Resorts in NSW and Victoria face a warm and dry start to the season with only sporadic falls of natural snow in many alpine areas

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Alpine ski resorts in New South Wales and Victoria saw climate records shattered at the weekend with maximum temperatures up to 12C above average.

Ski areas of Mount Hotham and Falls Creek set July records for their hottest daytime and night-time temperatures and Thredbo also set a new hottest July day, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.

Continue reading...
title: Australian ski resorts smash July climate records with temperatures 12C above average

description:
AMWU calls for wealth and inheritance taxes, free education and more revenue from gas companies as it outlines ‘working-class agenda’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A new tax rate for the highest income earners, introducing wealth and inheritance taxes and extracting more revenue from gas companies form part of a new leftwing manifesto circulating ahead of the Labor party’s national conference.

The extra tax revenue could help raise the jobseeker rate, make education – including university – free, and nationalise aged care under what the Australian Manufacturing Wo
title: Manufacturing union says Australia’s tax system is ‘rigged’ in bold manifesto ahead of Labor conference

author: Achol Arok
description:
Exclusive: TGA finds Touch Biotechnology test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea ‘is not reliable’ and has affected an unspecified number of people

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s only approved home test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea has been pulled from shelves after it failed to detect infections for an unspecified number of patients.

Touch Biotechnology has been handed a six‑month suspension by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) after a review of the company’s self‑testing kit found “the device is not reliable … and poses a high risk for false negative results for users”.
title: At-home STI test pulled from Australian shelves after failing to detect infections

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Bald eagle found hurt in California after fight with other birds, says group, as eagle called Jackie not seen on cameras

A beloved female bald eagle missing for several days in California’s Big Bear Lake is believed to have been found alive but injured after a fight with other birds, according to the advocacy group that operates a live, viral nestcam.

Friends of Bear Valley said on Facebook on Sunday that observers first spotted the eagle on the ground last Thursday, then witnessed it involved a “short ground altercation with two other subadult eagles” on Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Big Bear’s missing bald eagle believed to have been found alive but injured

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
US president says $400m plane will be ‘maxed out’ with appropriate protections but doesn’t give further details

Donald Trump acknowledged on Sunday that the Boeing jet given to him by Qatar cannot match the defensive armor of a true presidential aircraft, telling reporters it will soon be grounded so engineers can “max it out” with the protections it was never built with.

The admission came as Trump touched down in Washington on the jet, fresh off a trip to MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, where he handed the World Cup trophy to Spain alongside Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, after the tournament’s climactic final.

Continue reading...
title: Trump acknowledges that jet from Qatar lacks defensive systems of Air Force One

author: Steven Morris
description:
Jury at Winchester crown court told James Desborough was convicted in March of murdering Steven Kempster

A fan of a TV show about a serial killer strangled a cellmate in prison while awaiting trial for allegedly murdering two men and hiding their remains in Cornish woodland, a jury has heard.

James Desborough, 40, is accused of killing Claudio Aquilino and Daniel Coleman and concealing parts of their bodies in the dense undergrowth close to his cabin near St Austell.

Continue reading...
title: Double murder accused strangled HMP Exeter cellmate while awaiting trial

author: Martin Belam
description:
The US launches a ninth night of strikes targeting Iran. Plus, the glorious art deco LA Central Library celebrates 100 years

Good morning. The US launched a ninth night of strikes targeting Iran early Monday, after announcing the death of another American service member – the third in recent days. Donald Trump said the new attacks were “in honor” of the dead. Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned of “unforgettable lessons” if the US kept attacking.

Trump has threatened to target Iran’s power stations and bridges to try to compel Tehran to loosen its hold on the strait of Hormuz. Last week the US reimposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports. On Saturday, the military said it had redirected six ships and disabled one since then. Oil prices rose at the opening of trading in Asia on Monday, with the price of Brent crude climbing 2.72% to $90.50 a barrel.
title: First Thing: US continues attacks on Iran ‘in honor’ of dead service members | Martin Belam

author: Associated Press
description:
Defense department says 1Lt Tyler James Feehan of Hawaii and Pvt Isabella Gonzales of Texas were killed

The US military on Monday identified two soldiers killed in action recently as part of the war with Iran.

The defense department said in a statement that 1Lt Tyler James Feehan, 25, of Ewa Beach, Hawaii, and Pvt Isabella Gonzales, 19, of Carrollton, Texas, were killed in Jordan, where they were supporting a US mission against the Islamic State group. It is unclear how they were killed.

Continue reading...
title: US military identifies two soldiers killed in Iranian attack on Jordan

author: Reuters
description:
Spokesperson for Taylor Fresh Foods told Reuters ‌that the company was informed FDA made a mistake

  • What is the parasitic illness cyclosporiasis?

  • How to properly clean produce to help avoid cyclospora

The US Food and Drug ⁠Administration said on Sunday that laboratory experts re-checked lettuce sample results from Taylor Farms in an ⁠investigation into an ⁠outbreak of the ​cyclospora parasite and concluded the finding should be considered a false positive.

As of Sunday, there were ⁠no confirmed positive sample results for cyclospora, the FDA added. The FDA on Saturday had said that a ⁠sample of shredded iceberg lettuce s
title: FDA says review of Taylor Farms lettuce shows cyclospora finding was false positive

author: Tom Perkins
description:
EPA tosses out scientific research carried out under Biden and says toxic sludge not a significant threat to public

The Trump administration has killed proposed regulations for sewage sludge contaminated with Pfas and spread on farmland as fertilizer, a practice that has sickened farmers, destroyed their livelihoods, killed livestock,
title: Trump officials kill proposed rules for Pfas-contaminated sewage fertilizer

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Runcorn MP Sarah Pochin says parliament mounting ‘vicious and desperate campaign to stop Reform UK’

A Reform UK MP has complained that the standards system investigating Nigel Farage over undeclared gifts is a “kangaroo court”.

Sarah Pochin, the Runcorn MP, said Farage had called a byelection in his Clacton seat so voters could decide whether they backed him or not, and argued that “the media, the British state and the old parties have mounted a vicious and desperate campaign to stop Reform UK”.

Continue reading...
title: Investigation of Nigel Farage over undeclared gifts is ‘kangaroo court’, says Reform MP

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
New Labour leader takes over from Keir Starmer and will head to Downing Street to appoint his cabinet

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has formally become the UK prime minister after meeting King Charles at Buckingham Palace, the fourth person to hold the role in less than four years and the sixth within a decade.

Burnham, who took over from Keir Starmer as leader of the Labour party on Friday, accepted the appointment as prime minister shortly after Starmer had gone to the palace to resign to the monarch.

Conti
title: Andy Burnham becomes UK prime minister after meeting King Charles

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
OMB proposal would upend entire grant-making system – and put vast sums into hands of political appointees

It was a late Friday afternoon in Boston when Harvard School of Public Health professor Nancy Krieger, a social epidemiologist, received an email that would reshape the next year of her life.

It was from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) – her nearly $1m grant to study how discrimination affects population health was canceled.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Complete shock and dismay’: scientists unite against Trump’s $1tn grant attack

author: Lisa O’Carroll
description:
Chinese retail platform handed penalty over listings for items such as counterfeit products and unsafe toys

  • Business live – latest updates

AliExpress, the Chinese online retail platform, has been fined a record €550m (£470m) by the EU over its failure to stop illegal goods including harmful clothing, cosmetics and kitchen gadgets being sold through its site.

The European Commission fine is the biggest yet exacted by the bloc under the Digital Services Act (DSA), legislation that came into force in 2024, to protect consumers from illegal goods, deceptive or addictive marketing techniques.

Continue reading...
title: AliExpress fined record €550m by EU for failing to stop sale of illegal and fake goods

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Former state legislator in strong position to become Democratic candidate after several appointments drop out over the weekend

The US president, Donald Trump, has said the Qatari-donated jet that serves ⁠as an Air Force One plane will soon be sent away for “maxed out” upgrades, as concerns grow over the plane’s security features.

Trump started flying aboard ⁠the Boeing luxury jet on ⁠1 July ​after accepting the $400m plane as an “unconditional” gift from the Qatari government last year.

Continue reading...
title: Maine Democrats rally around Troy Jackson to replace Graham Platner in crucial Senate race – US politics live

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Senator says Trump revisiting failed run against Biden ‘distracts from important things’ such as Iran war

Rather than continue fixating on the 2020 election defeat that ended his first presidency, Donald Trump could instead “do something positive”, including resolving the US war in Iran, Pennsylvania senator John Fetterman said in an interview on Sunday.

“I don’t know why the president is dragging up all this stuff,” Fetterman remarked on CNN’s State of the Union, three days after Trump dedicated a televised, primetime address to claims about Chinese meddling in the 2020 White House race that he lost to Joe Biden. “You’re the president. Do something positive – and you are talking about 2020; that’s been settled over six years ago.
title: Trump could ‘do something positive’ rather than fixate on 2020 loss, Fetterman says

author: Dan Jervis-Bardy Chief political correspondent
description:
Statement by Israeli embassy in Canberra challenges proposed positions on settler violence and annexation of Palestinian territory

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Israel has made an intervention into the Labor party’s internal processes, publicly criticising a draft policy platform that it claims risks blaming Israel for the Gaza conflict while giving “insufficient attention” to the role of Hamas.

The Israeli embassy in Canberra issued a four-page statement on Monday challenging the proposed positions on Palestine, Hamas and settler violence in the West Bank, due to be debated at this week’s Labor national conference.
title: Israel criticises Labor’s draft Palestine policy in rare foreign intervention ahead of party conference

author: Kevin Rawlinson
description:
Corporation pays tribute to ‘outstanding’ journalist who presented shows including Today and One O’Clock News

The journalist Edward Stourton has died aged 68, it has been announced.

The BBC Radio 4 presenter was best known for fronting current affairs programmes including Today, World at One and its religious and ethical current affairs series Sunday.

Continue reading...
title: BBC broadcaster Edward Stourton dies aged 68

author: Christopher Knaus
description:
Catholic order with a record of child abuse could be subject to hundreds of redress claims worth up to $65m

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian taxpayers could be forced to cover up to $65m in payouts to hundreds of abuse victims when a failing arm of the Catholic church disappears, new court documents reveal.

Last month, the Christian Brothers, a Catholic order with a shocking record of child abuse,
title: Taxpayers could pay millions to abuse survivors if Christian Brothers goes bankrupt, court documents reveal

description:
Former attorney general also describes receiving antisemitic abuse, saying he was labelled a ‘genocidal Zionist’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former attorney general Mark Dreyfus has called on governments to consider banning protests outside synagogues and Jewish schools, invoking a high court decision allowing restrictions outside abortion clinics.

The federal Labor backbencher has told the royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion th
title: Ban on protests outside synagogues and Jewish schools should be considered, Dreyfus tells royal commission

description:
Many of the more than 100 people awaiting processing on the tiny Pacific island are skipping meals to make ends meet, a new survey has found

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Most refugees and asylum seekers held in Nauru’s detention centres say they cannot afford to buy enough food or access clean drinking water, despite the Australian government spending the equivalent of more than $9m per person last financial year.

The group of more than 100 peopl
title: Australia spent more than $9m for each asylum seeker held on Nauru last year – so why can’t they afford to buy food?

author: Josh Butler
description:
Lee Hanson claims her mother’s comments on Tommy Robinson podcast were ‘misinterpreted’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Barnaby Joyce says Pauline Hanson does not support the White Australia policy but he has backed her support for “mass deportations” of those overstaying their visas.

Hanson and her colleagues have spent days clarifying, explaining or walking back headline-grabbing parts of
title: Barnaby Joyce says One Nation doesn’t want return of White Australia policy but backs Pauline Hanson on mass deportations

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
After the US military confirmed that a service member had been killed in Iraq – the third in recent days – Donald Trump said the new attacks were ‘in honour’ of the dead

  • Middle East crisis live: follow latest updates

The US launched a ninth night of strikes targeting Iran early Monday, after announcing the death of another American service member, as the price of Brent crude oil climbed above $90 a barrel, the highest level since June.

The US military said the service member was killed on Saturday in northern Iraq, where the US has military bases, during a controlled detonation of what was called unexploded ordnance on a downed Iranian attack drone.

Continue reading...
title: US launches ninth night of Iran strikes as strait of Hormuz standoff sees oil price pass $90 a barrel
